title: Import the company remote-development workspace into the Try Omarchy VM

statements.text: The confirmed rdev session cluster imports from the macOS host opencode store into the Try Omarchy VM live store via row-scoped export (session rows plus messages and parts), re-homed to the migrated project directories; no whole-store copy.

The triaged rdev worktree set migrates as full self-contained copies under the VM project root: a full clone per unit checked out on its source branch, with uncommitted state carried as patches and stashes and verified by status parity; dangling linked-worktree filesystem copies are not migrated.
The company workspace repository migrates as one full clone under the VM project root, and the handoff note documents its relevant rdev branch inventory.
A handoff note records the old-to-new path map, per-unit carried WIP, and the remaining operator steps: workspace mise tooling install, one gcloud authentication, session resume.

Every artifact in this repository is company-anonymized: no organization names, company repository names, session identifiers, or tab-fork labels appear in tracked files; the repository publication identifier test passes.
No company credentials, tokens, or session content enter this public repository; imported session rows stay in the VM-private store.
Destination root is the VM project directory (established flat kebab-case convention); migrated units keep their source slugs, lowercased and kebab-cased where needed.
Session import uses the established transplant machinery (row-scoped export plus project re-homing), not raw file copies of the store.

The rdev forks resolve to tab-fork sessions and rdev/workspace-dotfiles branches inside the company workspace repository, not standalone remote repositories; build triage verifies this against the host store before import.

The two operator-named session identifiers matched no row in any inspected store (host live store, host personal store, VM store); the final set is enumerated from title candidates and confirmed with the operator at build start. A wrong import is reversible by row deletion.
The host opencode store is 91 GB; exports must be row-scoped and size-checked per session to bound transfer time and VM store growth.
Dirty-state carry may not re-apply bit-for-bit onto fresh clones; patches and stashes are exported separately and the handoff note records status-parity results.
No cloud company VM access and no gcloud authentication inside this initiative; the operator authenticates once after migration.
No bulk migration of the historical worktree sprawl beyond the triaged rdev set; the host external volume remains the deep backup.
No new managed tooling in this repository and no changes to the retired darwin workstation stack.
Fold the VM project-root convention into the personal dotfiles as declarative state in a future initiative.
